source.anchor_kjv: I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.
source.thread: Psalm 22 does not end at the cross — at verse 22 the forsaken sufferer turns from anguish to praise, standing alive in the midst of the congregation. Hebrews 2:12 takes that very opening line and puts it in the mouth of the RISEN Christ, and Hebrews 2:11 says He is not ashamed to call them brethren. Cross -> resurrection -> family: the risen Christ calls you in.
source.thread_lever: NT-confirmed OT echo (Hebrews 2:12 cites Ps 22:22 of the risen Christ; resurrection NT-warranted)
source.hook_line: Most people stop reading Psalm twenty-two at the cross.
source.spoken_script: Most people stop reading Psalm twenty-two at the cross. Keep going — it doesn't end in a grave. But the cry doesn't stay forsaken. Later, the psalm turns — the same voice moves from anguish to praise: "I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee." Who is that praising voice? Hebrews takes that opening line — word for word — and puts it in the mouth of the risen Christ. The psalm's turn is Jesus, alive on the far side of the cross. And hear what He calls us. Hebrews says He is — "not ashamed to call them brethren" — brothers. Family. The same Jesus who cried out forsaken now lives — and the risen Christ is not ashamed to call His own brethren. He is calling you into that family.

platforms.title: Most People Stop Reading Psalm 22 at the Cross. Keep Going.
platforms.description:
Most people stop reading Psalm 22 at the cross. But the psalm doesn't end there.

At verse 22, the same voice that cried "forsaken" turns to praise:

Psalm 22:22 (KJV): "I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee."

Who is that praising voice? Hebrews 2:12 takes that exact line and puts it in the mouth of the risen Christ. The psalm's turn is Jesus, alive on the far side of the cross.

And hear what He calls us: Hebrews says He is not ashamed to call us brethren. Brothers. Family.

He was forsaken so you could be family. The risen Christ is calling you in.

Scripture quoted from the King James Version (KJV), public domain.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Psalm 22 Does Not End at the Cross - The Turn to Resurrection and Family
platforms.description:
Most people stop reading Psalm 22 at the cross. That's where they miss the most important turn in the whole passage.

At verse 22, the voice of the forsaken sufferer pivots from anguish to praise:

Psalm 22:22 (KJV): "I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee."

Who is that praising voice? The New Testament answers it directly. Hebrews 2:12 takes that exact opening line and quotes it as the words of the risen Christ. The psalm's turn - from dereliction to praise - is the resurrection. Jesus is the voice speaking on the far side of the cross.

And then Hebrews 2:11 adds something that should stop you in your tracks: he is not ashamed to call them brethren. The risen Jesus calls his own - brothers. Family.

Cross. Resurrection. Family. The whole arc is in Psalm 22 if you keep reading.

Psalm 22 | Hebrews 2 | KJV

Subscribe to walk through the whole Bible and meet Jesus on every page. ✝

Scripture quoted from the King James Version (KJV), public domain.
